tools.description:
Search Notion pages and databases, or look up a user by name or email. Does not search connected apps; use connector_search, when listed, for sources such as Slack, Google Drive, GitHub, mail, or calendar. When connector_search is listed, call it in parallel with search on the first search for an information need, unless the user names a source, the request is a user lookup, or the request is about Notion pages or databases themselves, such as finding a page to read or edit. Decisions, status updates, and discussions often live in connected sources. Preserve distinctive names and identifiers.

Use a non-empty query for content searches. Leave the query empty only when you also send filters or a non-relevance sort, as in the browse example below. Omit optional parameters unless needed. Do not add filters or sorting just to fill in defaults. Business or Enterprise is required for filters.edited_by_user_ids, filters.last_edited_date_range, filters.title_only=true, filters.content_status, more than one distinct teamspace across teamspace_id and filters.teamspace_ids, and sort other than relevance. On other plans, those options are dropped with a notice in the result, and results may be broader. Keep filters nested inside "filters". Use YYYY-MM-DD for start_date and end_date. Use page_size, not limit.

For user lookup, set query_type="user" and provide a name or email. A document about a person is a content search, not a user lookup.

<example description="Find a page by title">
{"query":"Q3 roadmap"}
</example>
<example description="Browse pages you edited most recently">
{"query":"","filters":{"edited_by_user_ids":["me"]},"sort":"last_edited"}
</example>
<example description="Find a user">
{"query":"[REDACTED]","query_type":"user"}
</example>
tools.name: notion-search

tools.description: Search memories that the user's connected agents saved in earlier sessions: context, preferences, corrections, and decisions. Returns the best matches, not every memory. To list, count, or filter memories, fetch id "memory" and run query-data-sources on its data source. The first time you use memory in a conversation, whether searching or saving, read [REDACTED] once.
tools.name: notion-memory-search

tools.description: Inspect current tool availability, parameter restrictions, and recovery links when diagnosing an access problem or when the user asks about access. For routine work, call the tool you need directly; no access precheck is required. Tool results report access denials and recovery steps for the calling account. Call with {} for the full access map, or pass tool_names, for example ["search", "connector_search"], to narrow the result. Reuse access information already in context, but the operation's result is authoritative if access changes. Use tools marked "available". Use tools marked "available_with_limit" within their limits. It shows one of two content-search setups. Unified search: use ai_search when it is available, including user lookup with query_type="user", and search is then omitted; otherwise use search. Split search: ai_search is omitted, search covers Notion pages, databases, and user lookup, and connector_search covers connected sources such as Slack or Google Drive. connector_search needs AI search access and a connected source to return results. A listed tool may still be restricted for the calling account. Tool availability and restricted_parameters are independent: omit restricted options even when the tool is available. Unknown names and tools not exposed to this connection are omitted. This tool does not grant access or change the workspace.
tools.name: notion-get-tool-access

tools.description:
Retrieves details about a Notion entity (page, database, data source, or saved database view) by URL or ID.

Provide a URL or ID in `id`. Make multiple calls for multiple entities.

For pages, use path, verification, edit time, and truncation metadata to assess the source. Treat recency as context, not proof. Report material uncertainty when sources conflict.

Pages use Notion-flavored Markdown. For the complete specification, read the MCP resource `[REDACTED]` through your MCP client's resource-reading interface, or call the Notion "fetch" tool with this URI if your client does not support reading MCP resources. Do NOT pass this URI to any other URL-fetching tool.

Pass a `[REDACTED]` URI as `id` to read that MCP documentation resource.

Databases return data sources in `<data-source url="[REDACTED]">` tags. Fetch the collection:// URL for its schema and use it with update_data_source or query_data_sources. Multi-source databases return more than one data source.

Saved views return filters, sorts, and display settings. To query their rows, use query_data_sources with `mode: "view"`.

A null cover or icon means none; an omitted one means unavailable, not absent. Keep a page's Markdown icon attribute for edit round trips. File URLs expire; re-fetch to refresh them. Uploaded media blocks use stable `notion-file-block://` sources; keep them when editing or copying Markdown. Get download URLs with get_file_download_urls, or set `include_file_urls` to true for a `references` map. Before relying on page content, check `truncated`, `unknown_block_count`, and `unknown_block_ids` for omitted subtrees.

Set `include_discussions` to true for discussion counts, markers, previews, and `discussion://` URLs that correlate with get_comments.
tools.name: notion-fetch

tools.description:
Create an attachment and upload it to Notion.

Provide exactly one source:
- content for small UTF-8 text artifacts such as HTML, Markdown, plain text, CSV, JSON, XML, CSS, YAML, TSV, calendar, GPX, or SVG files.
- source_url for a direct, publicly reachable HTTPS file URL.
- source_file_id for a file this exact integration already uploaded. When create_file_upload is available, use it for local files so the upload has the same owner.


For content and source_url, filename must use a supported extension and content_type must agree with it. Omit content_type to infer it. source_file_id takes neither because the stored upload carries both. For larger files, redirects, or authenticated downloads, upload through the Notion File Upload API with this integration's token and pass source_file_id.

The response includes a markdown_source value. To place the uploaded file on a page, pass that source to create-pages or update-page. To attach it to a comment, include suggested_markdown on a separate line in create-comment markdown. Unattached uploads remain temporary and are deleted once they expire: content and source_url open a fresh one-hour window, while source_file_id keeps the window that opened when the file was first uploaded, so place that source promptly and upload the file again if it has already expired. "HTML", "HTML block", "HTML artifact", and "HTML embed" all mean an HTML file placed with <embed source="[REDACTED]" /> so Notion renders the sandboxed preview. Never place HTML in a code block or file block. Use <file source="[REDACTED]" /> for other files.
tools.name: notion-create-attachment

tools.description:
Create a short-lived URL for uploading one local file directly to Notion.

After calling this tool, send exactly one multipart/form-data POST request to `upload_url`. Put the file in the `file` form field and include every header returned in `upload_headers`. Files are limited to 20 MiB for this single-part upload flow, and workspace file-size limits still apply.

The upload response includes `markdown_source` and `suggested_markdown`, which can be passed directly to create-pages or update-page, or included on a separate line in create-comment markdown to attach the file. The URL is short-lived, can upload only the FileUpload created by this call, and runs as this same integration.

<examples>
1. Prepare an image upload: {"filename":"diagram.png"}
2. Prepare a PDF upload with an explicit MIME type: {"filename":"report.pdf","content_type":"application/pdf"}
</examples>
tools.name: notion-create-file-upload

tools.description:
Download the contents of a small UTF-8 text attachment created by the Notion MCP `create-attachment` tool.

Pass the `file_upload_id` returned by `create-attachment`. The attachment must belong to the requesting integration, have completed uploading, and use a supported text format such as HTML, Markdown, plain text, CSV, JSON, XML, CSS, YAML, TSV, calendar, GPX, or SVG.

The response contains the complete text in `content` so you can save it locally, edit it, and call `create-attachment` again to upload a new version. Downloads are limited to 200 KiB. This tool does not fetch arbitrary URLs or return binary files. For larger or binary attachments, use the signed file URL returned when reading the containing Notion page.

<examples>
1. Download a text attachment: {"file_upload_id":"[REDACTED]"}
</examples>
tools.name: notion-download-attachment

tools.description:
Get signed download URLs for files that fetch output cites by stable `notion-file-block://` references.

Pass up to 25 references exactly as they appear in the page Markdown. Each reference resolves independently: `files` lists the ones that resolved and `unresolved` lists the rest with a reason. The URLs expire after a few minutes; call this tool again for fresh ones. Keep the stable references, not the URLs, when editing or copying page Markdown.

<examples>
1. Get download URLs: {"references":["[REDACTED]"]}
</examples>
tools.name: notion-get-file-download-urls

tools.description:
Creates one or more Notion pages with the specified properties and content.

## Core rules

**IMPORTANT**: Before writing page content, read the MCP resource `[REDACTED]` through your MCP client's resource-reading interface, or call the Notion "fetch" tool with this URI if your client does not support reading MCP resources. Do NOT pass this URI to any other URL-fetching tool. Do NOT invent Markdown syntax. Put the page title in properties, not content. By default, use native Notion mentions for references you add to existing Notion pages, databases, data sources, people, and dates. Use Markdown links only for external URLs or when the user requests a plain link. For a person, use a user mention with their user URL, found with search using query_type "user"; do not write "@Name" as plain text. For a specific date or time, such as a due date or meeting time, use a date mention. The Markdown specification gives the mention syntax.

Use a named destination as parent. Otherwise use "creation_mode": "draft" for a durable private page. Do not combine draft mode with parent, or move or share it without direction.

For a meeting note, use create_meeting_note if available, even in a Meetings database, unless the user wants a regular page.

For a database, ALWAYS fetch first. Use its collection:// URL as data_source_id, exact property names, and title property. Never put a database ID in page_id. Outside a database, the only allowed property is the required "title".



For reusable instructions, set "is_skill": true. Before creating a skill, read the MCP resource `[REDACTED]` through your MCP client's resource-reading interface. If your client does not support reading MCP resources, call the Notion "fetch" tool with this URI instead. Do NOT pass this URI to any other URL-fetching tool. Do not mark ordinary pages or drafts as skills. Report any "warnings" in the result to the user.
tools.name: notion-create-pages

tools.description:
Update a Notion page's properties, content, icon, or cover. For only an icon or cover, use "update_properties" without "properties".

## Core rules

**IMPORTANT**: Before writing page content, read the MCP resource `[REDACTED]` through your MCP client's resource-reading interface, or call the Notion "fetch" tool with this URI if your client does not support reading MCP resources. Do NOT pass this URI to any other URL-fetching tool. Don't guess Markdown syntax. By default, use native Notion mentions for references you add to existing Notion pages, databases, data sources, people, and dates. Use Markdown links only for external URLs or when the user requests a plain link. For a person, use a user mention with their user URL, found with search using query_type "user"; do not write "@Name" as plain text. For a specific date or time, such as a due date or meeting time, use a date mention. The Markdown specification gives the mention syntax.

Before changing content, fetch unless already loaded. Match nearby headings, block types, nesting, lists, tables, and prose style.

Make the smallest edit. Use "update_content" for targeted search-and-replace and "insert_content" only to prepend or append. Avoid "replace_content" when a targeted command works. Preserve unrelated wording, structure, order, and native references. Do not broadly rewrite unless asked.

For "update_content", use the smallest exact old_str that uniquely matches the target. Ask before removing material content the user did not identify. Don't fetch just to verify an update that completed without warnings. Fetch to resolve warnings, or when a later step needs the page's exact saved state.

For "replace_content", preserve child pages and databases with their exact fetched tags. If validation says child content would be deleted, show the list and ask first. Never retry with "allow_deleting_content": true without confirmation. Report any "warnings" in the result.
tools.name: notion-update-page

tools.description: Move Notion pages to Trash. They can be restored with the restore_pages tool or from Trash in Notion. Database rows are pages. To move a database to Trash, use delete_databases. To remove content inside a page, use update_page instead. Use this tool only when the user explicitly asks to delete specific pages. Never use it on your own initiative to clean up, deduplicate, or reorganize content. Without [REDACTED]: true, nothing is trashed and the error lists what would be moved to Trash; show that list to the user and retry only after they confirm.
tools.name: notion-delete-pages

tools.description: Move Notion databases to Trash. They can be restored with the restore_pages tool or from Trash in Notion. Each database goes to Trash with all of its rows. Pass a full-page or inline database that owns its data, not a linked view. To move a page or database row to Trash, use delete_pages. Use this tool only when the user explicitly asks to delete specific databases. Never use it on your own initiative to clean up, deduplicate, or reorganize content. Without [REDACTED]: true, nothing is trashed and the error lists what would be moved to Trash; show that list to the user and retry only after they confirm.
tools.name: notion-delete-databases

tools.description: Restore Notion pages or databases from Trash to where they were before they were deleted. Use this when the user asks to undo a deletion or to restore something from Trash. Database rows are pages. Restoring something that is already out of Trash succeeds and changes nothing. To restore a page whose parent is in Trash, restore the parent.
tools.name: notion-restore-pages

tools.description: Mark an existing Notion page as a skill without changing its content. The page must be in the current workspace, and the authenticated user must have permission to edit it. Use this tool only when the user wants the page's current contents designated as a skill.
tools.name: notion-convert-page-to-skill

tools.description: Import a spec-compliant Agent Skills directory into a page in a Skills database. First call action=prepare with page_id and the exact tar.gz content_length and checksum_crc32. PUT the raw archive bytes to upload_url with all upload_headers, then call action=complete with the same page_id and upload_token. The archive must contain SKILL.md with name/description YAML frontmatter, either at the root or in a single matching skill-name directory. Completion replaces the page title, Description, body, and Files; it preserves the page and uses the page-update diff engine rather than recreating all content blocks. SKILL.md becomes page content. Its sibling folders and files are added directly to Files, preserving nested directories without a skill-name wrapper. Previous folders are not deleted. For a new skill, create a page in a Skills database first. Maximum 20 MiB compressed, 25 MiB expanded, 1000 entries, 20 path levels, and 200 UTF-8 bytes per filename. Paths must be unique ignoring case. Only name and description are imported from frontmatter; optional fields are ignored. Links and special files are rejected. Upload URLs and tokens expire after ten minutes. Uploading never executes skill instructions or scripts.
tools.name: notion-upload-skill

tools.description: Download a spec-compliant Notion Skill as a complete tar.gz archive containing SKILL.md and its supporting files and nested folders. Pass the skill page ID. Returns a temporary signed url. Download and extract the archive to read or use the skill.
tools.name: notion-download-skill

tools.description: Use this tool to view the Notion skills the user has enabled for you and other external MCP clients, each with a name and a description of when it should be used. If you choose to use one of these skills, mention to the user that you are loading the skill from Notion first, then download them.
tools.name: notion-get-enabled-skills

tools.description: Update the current user's settings for one Notion Skill. Enable or disable the Skill, control automatic use, configure where it is shown, or enable use in connected MCP agents. Omitted settings remain unchanged. This does not run the Skill.
tools.name: notion-update-skill-settings

tools.description: Records when you have completed a guided set up flow of the Notion MCP. Only call this tool when explicitly asked.
tools.name: notion-complete-mcp-setup

tools.description: Move one or more Notion pages or databases to a new parent. People can gain or lose access because moved items inherit access from the new parent.
tools.name: notion-move-pages

tools.description: Duplicate a Notion page. The page must be within the current workspace, and you must have permission to access it. The duplication completes asynchronously, so do not rely on the new page identified by the returned ID or URL to be populated immediately. Let the user know that the duplication is in progress and that they can check back later using the 'fetch' tool or by clicking the returned URL and viewing it in the Notion app.
tools.name: notion-duplicate-page

tools.description:
Creates a new Notion database using SQL DDL syntax, or a canonical typed database for tasks, projects, or skills.

Provide exactly one of:
- schema: a CREATE TABLE statement. If no title property is provided, "Name" is auto-added.
- database_type: one of tasks, projects, or skills. The database is created with the canonical required properties and typed metadata used by Notion.


For schema, use CREATE TABLE with double-quoted column names and single-quoted type options. If no title property is provided, "Name" is auto-added.

Property type syntax:
- Simple: TITLE, RICH_TEXT, DATE, PEOPLE, CHECKBOX, URL, EMAIL, PHONE_NUMBER, FILES
- SELECT('opt':color, ...) / MULTI_SELECT('opt':color, ...)
- Option names can't contain commas: use '$1000+', not '$1,000+'. List separate options as 'A', 'B', not 'A, B'.
- STATUS('Backlog':gray:to_do, 'Building':blue:in_progress, 'Shipped':green:complete); groups are to_do, in_progress, complete
- NUMBER [FORMAT 'dollar'] / FORMULA('expression')
- RELATION('ds') for a one-way relation
- RELATION('ds', DUAL) for a two-way relation
- RELATION('ds', DUAL 'Children') with a synced property name
- RELATION('ds', DUAL 'Children' 'children') with a synced name and synced_id (for self-relations)
- ROLLUP('rel_prop', 'target_prop', 'function')
- UNIQUE_ID [PREFIX 'WEB-BUG'] / CREATED_TIME / LAST_EDITED_TIME
- UNIQUE_ID PREFIX: 2-10 characters, a letter then letters, digits, or hyphens (e.g. 'TASK-ID', not 'TASK_ID' or 'T'). Each prefix can be used by only one data source per workspace, so prefer a specific prefix like 'WEB-BUG' over 'TASK'.
- Any column: COMMENT 'description text' Colors: default, gray, brown, orange, yellow, green, blue, purple, pink, red.


Returns Markdown with schema, SQLite definition, and data source ID in <data-source> tag for use with update_data_source and query_data_sources tools.
tools.name: notion-create-database

tools.description:
Creates an empty Notion Folder. Set parent.page_id for a top-level Folder owned by a page, or parent.folder_id to create a nested Folder inside another Folder. A page-owned Folder is not inserted into the page's content. A nested Folder is appended to its parent Folder's content. The Folder inherits access from its parent.

This tool creates only the empty Folder. It is non-idempotent and creates a new Folder on every successful call.
tools.name: notion-create-folder
notion-update-folder

tools.description:
Update a Notion data source's schema, title, attributes, or page layout. Schema changes use SQL DDL statements. Returns Markdown showing updated structure and schema.

Accepts a data source ID (collection ID from fetch response's <data-source> tag) or a single-source database ID. Multi-source databases require the specific data source ID.

The statements param accepts semicolon-separated DDL statements:
- ADD COLUMN "Name" <type> - add a new property
- DROP COLUMN "Name" - remove a property
- RENAME COLUMN "Old" TO "New" - rename a property
- ALTER COLUMN "Name" SET <type> - change type/options. For SELECT, MULTI_SELECT, and STATUS, list every option to keep; omitted options are removed. Existing options keep their id and can be recolored. STATUS options keep their group when the group is omitted.


The page_layout param replaces the layout every page in the data source uses (pinned properties, sidebar, property sections, and a content tab next to views). Fetch the data source first to get the current layout, then edit it. See [REDACTED] for the format.

Notes: Cannot delete/create title properties. Max one unique_id property. Cannot update synced databases. Use "fetch" first to see current schema and get the data source ID from <data-source url="[REDACTED]"> tags.
tools.name: notion-update-data-source

tools.description:
Add a comment to a page or specific content.

Provide `page_id` to identify the page, then choose ONE targeting mode:
- `page_id` alone: Add a top-level comment to the page
- `page_id` + `selection_with_ellipsis`: Highlight selected text within one block, or comment on the block where the match starts if no inline highlight can be resolved. No matching content returns an error.
- `reply_to_comment_id`: Reply to a comment using its `id` from get-comments (page_id is still required)
- `discussion_id`: Reply to an existing discussion (page_id is still required)


Provide exactly one content format:
- `rich_text`: Array of rich text objects.
tools.name: notion-create-comment

tools.description:
Get comments and discussions from a Notion page.

Returns page-level and inline discussions in XML format. Long results are shortened:
- If `shown-count` is less than `total-count`, some discussions were left out. Up to 50 are listed as `<omitted-discussion id="[REDACTED]"/>`: pass that URL as `discussion_id` to fetch it. If `omitted-truncated="true"`, more were left out; `fetch` with `include_discussions: true` may show their URLs.
- Each discussion has `comment-count` (comments shown) and `total-comment-count`. A discussion that does not fit keeps its newest comments. When older comments were left out, it has `next-cursor`: pass it as `cursor` with that `discussion_id` to get the next older comments. Repeat until a response has no `next-cursor`. If it has `reactions-truncated="true"`, some of its reactions were left out to fit. On supported Business connections, pending suggested edits use `kind="suggested_edit"` and their `discussion://` URL can be passed to `get_suggested_edit`. Resolved suggestions stay retired. Check `suggested_edits_status` to distinguish an empty result from unavailable suggestion discovery. Comments you wrote have `by-you="true"`.


Tip: Use the `fetch` tool with `include_discussions: true` first to see where discussions are anchored in the page content, then use this tool to retrieve full discussion threads. The `discussion://` URLs in the fetch output match the discussion IDs returned here.

Parameters:
- `include_resolved`: Include resolved discussions (default: false)
- `discussion_id`: Fetch a specific discussion by ID or URL
- `cursor`: A discussion's `next-cursor`, to get its older comments (requires `discussion_id`)


<example>{"page_id": "page-uuid"}</example>
<example>{"page_id": "page-uuid", "discussion_id": "[REDACTED]"}</example>
<example>{"page_id": "page-uuid", "discussion_id": "[REDACTED]", "cursor": "comment-uuid"}</example>
tools.name: notion-get-comments

tools.description: Replace the text of a comment you wrote. Get the comment ID from get_comments or create_comment. The new text replaces the whole comment, so send the full corrected text. To fix a comment, update it instead of deleting it and posting a new one. You can only edit your own comments.
tools.name: notion-update-comment

tools.description: Delete a comment you wrote. Get the comment ID from get_comments or create_comment. If it is the last comment in its discussion, the discussion is removed too. Use this only when the user asks to delete a comment; to fix a comment, use update_comment instead. You can only delete your own comments.
tools.name: notion-delete-comment

tools.description: Resolve or reopen a comment discussion. Get the discussion ID from get_comments or create_comment. Use this tool only when a human explicitly asks to resolve that discussion. Do not infer resolution from addressing feedback, replying, completing related work, passing checks, or changing task status.
tools.name: notion-set-discussion-resolved

tools.description: Add or remove your emoji reaction on a comment. Get the comment ID from get_comments or create_comment. Safe to repeat: setting the same state twice changes nothing.
tools.name: notion-set-comment-reaction

tools.description:
Propose one precise, reviewable change without changing accepted page content. Copy old_text exactly from fetch, use one suggestion per localized change, and use get_suggested_edit to inspect it before any later resolution.

Requires a Business or Enterprise workspace plan. Call this tool directly. If access is denied, follow the recovery guidance in the result.
tools.name: notion-create-suggested-edit

tools.description:
Read the exact before-and-after diff and currently allowed actions for one pending suggested edit. Call this before deciding whether to accept or reject it.

Requires a Business or Enterprise workspace plan. Call this tool directly. If access is denied, follow the recovery guidance in the result.
tools.name: notion-get-suggested-edit

tools.description:
Accept or reject one pending suggested edit. Use the exact suggested_edit_url, inspect it with get_suggested_edit first, and call this only after the user explicitly chooses accept or reject.

Requires a Business or Enterprise workspace plan. Call this tool directly. If access is denied, follow the recovery guidance in the result.
tools.name: notion-resolve-suggested-edit

tools.description:
Retrieves the current status of an async task that was started by another tool (for example, "create_pages" called with "allow_async": true).

The status is one of "queued", "running", "retrying", "succeeded", or "failed". When the task has succeeded, the operation's result is included; when it has failed, an error is included instead.

Poll this tool with the "task_id" from the original tool's "async_task" response. Wait briefly between polls — the original response includes a suggested backoff.

<examples>
1. Check a task's status: {"task_id": "task_abc123"}
</examples>
tools.name: notion-get-async-task
notion-get-teams
notion-get-groups
notion-get-users

tools.description:
Query data source rows, SQL, or a saved view.

Use the required top-level `data` object. Do not pass query parameters at the top level.

First fetch every data source's schema and collection:// URL.

Missing-column recovery: try a schema-backed error suggestion or refetch. If correction fails, next call MUST be fetch, NOT SQL, even with new hints. Rebuild from current `<sqlite-table>`; never guess names/IDs.

Modes (default: sql):
- rows preserves mentions, links, formatting, dates, and equations. Use before rich-text repairs/rewrites.
- sql runs read-only SQLite. No `VALUES`; inline rows: `WITH "ids"("x") AS (SELECT 'a' UNION ALL SELECT 'b')`. Use only table/column names in fetched `<sqlite-table>`, never property IDs. Schema keys name properties; schema/view listings (e.g. `displayProperties`) may be unqueryable. Formula/rollup columns must be listed; otherwise use rows/fetch. System `url`/`createdTime` are columns; other metadata must be listed. Never guess `Name`, `Title`, `page_id`, `rowid`, `lastEditedTime`. User `url`/`id` use `userDefined:` columns (e.g. `"userDefined:url"`). Date properties expand to `date:<Name>:start`, `:end`, `:is_datetime`; `created_time` keeps its base name. Bind untrusted values with `?` and `params`. Include needed filters; view filters don't apply. SQL may omit mentions/formatting and link destinations. This is not proof of corrupt properties.
- view runs saved filters/sorts. is_archived defaults false (active); true selects archived rows. If has_more, pass next_cursor as start_cursor with the same is_archived.


Rows `limit` and view `page_size` are integers 1-100. Examples: `[REDACTED]`.

View mode has no tool-specific plan quota. SQL is unlimited on Business and Enterprise with Notion AI. Other plans have a shared workspace limit for single-data-source SQL and cannot query multiple data sources at once. Call this tool directly. If a SQL limit is reached, follow the guidance in the result or use a saved view.
tools.name: notion-query-data-sources

tools.description:
Query data across multiple Notion data sources using read-only SQLite SQL.

Use this tool for JOINs, UNIONs, comparisons, and aggregations that need two or more data sources. Queries across multiple data sources require a Business or Enterprise plan with Notion AI. Call this tool directly. If access is denied, follow the recovery guidance in the result. Use query_data_sources instead when you need one data source or a saved database view.

Prerequisites:
1. Use the "fetch" tool first to get each data source's schema and collection:// URL.
2. Data source URLs are found in <data-source url="..."> tags in fetch results.


SQL:
- Use each collection:// URL as a quoted SQLite table name in the query.
- Bind untrusted values with ? placeholders and params; do not interpolate them into SQL.
- Include every needed filter in WHERE. Saved-view filters and sorts are not automatically applied.
- Checkbox values: use "__YES__" for checked and "__NO__" for unchecked.
- Date properties expand to `date:<Name>:start`, `:end`, `:is_datetime`; `created_time` keeps its base name.


Returns matching rows, the queried data source IDs, and whether results were truncated.
tools.name: notion-query-multiple-data-sources

tools.description:
Query the current user's meeting notes data source.


Treat words such as summaries, notes, todos, action items, and deliverables as requested meeting output, not title terms. Example: "What are my meeting todos?" needs no title filter for "todos". Add a title filter only when the user clearly names a meeting, such as "standup", "sprint planning", or "1:1 with Alice". Generic date phrases like "recent meetings", "latest meetings", "meetings this week", or "yesterday's meetings" should be interpreted as date range filters — never as title filters. Unless the user asks about a meeting whose title contains another person's name, treat that person as an attendee or creator. Use their name as a title fallback only after attendee filtering returns no results.

Title keyword matching is case-insensitive; capitalization does not matter. Matching is lexical, so simplify a filter to one term when it returns no results. The filter parameter contains the complete property, date, Boolean-combination, and example reference.

Requires AI meeting notes access and workspace enablement. Call this tool directly. If access is denied, follow the recovery guidance in the result.
tools.name: notion-query-meeting-notes

tools.description: List the current user's top-level pages and databases in their Private sidebar section. Use this to browse private workspace structure. For content searches, including keywords and titles, use search. Use connector_search, when listed, for connected sources. Follow cursor pagination when the complete list is needed.
tools.name: notion-list-private-pages

tools.description: List pages and databases in the current user's Shared sidebar section. Use this to browse content shared directly with the user. For content searches, including keywords and titles, use search. Use connector_search, when listed, for connected sources. Follow cursor pagination when the complete list is needed.
tools.name: notion-list-shared-pages

tools.description: List the current user's favorite pages and databases in sidebar order. Use this when the user refers to a favorite or pinned workspace item. Follow cursor pagination when the complete list is needed.
tools.name: notion-list-favorite-pages

tools.description: List pages and databases the current user recently viewed, ranked by recency and visit frequency. Use this to recover likely navigation context when the user refers to something they were recently working on. This reflects views, not edits; to find pages the user edited, use search with filters.edited_by_user_ids: ["me"] and sort: "last_edited". Follow cursor pagination when the complete list is needed.
tools.name: notion-list-recent-pages

tools.description:
Search agents by name or description, or browse the current user's favorite agents and the workspace's newest agents. Queries return one page. Without a query, follow nextCursor until it is omitted, even when a bounded workspace page is empty. Use this instead of list_agents when personal favorites or relevance-ranked search are needed.

Requires Notion AI and Custom Agents access. Call this tool directly. If access is denied, follow the recovery guidance in the result.
tools.name: notion-search-agents

tools.description:
Search past agent sessions by topic in a periodically refreshed index and return matching session URLs and excerpts. Recently created or updated sessions may not appear; use query_sessions for recent sessions.

Requires Notion AI and Custom Agents access. Call this tool directly. If access is denied, follow the recovery guidance in the result.
tools.name: notion-search-sessions

tools.description:
List agent sessions available to the integration. Filter, sort, or search by title. A bounded page can be empty while has_more is true; follow next_cursor until has_more is false.

Requires Notion AI and Custom Agents access. Call this tool directly. If access is denied, follow the recovery guidance in the result.
tools.name: notion-query-sessions

tools.description:
Start a session with a published Custom Agent. Use get_session_status or wait_session to check its progress.

Requires Notion AI and Custom Agents access. Call this tool directly. If access is denied, follow the recovery guidance in the result.

tools.description:

Requires Notion AI and Custom Agents access. Call this tool directly. If access is denied, follow the recovery guidance in the result.
tools.name: notion-get-session-status

tools.description:
Wait for the latest turn in a Custom Agent session to stop running.

Requires Notion AI and Custom Agents access. Call this tool directly. If access is denied, follow the recovery guidance in the result.

tools.description:
Create a new view on a Notion database.

Use fetch first to get database_id, parent_page_id, and the collection:// data_source_id. The caller needs edit access to the database or parent page and access to the data source.

Provide exactly one placement: database_id adds a view tab to that database; parent_page_id appends an inline linked database view to that page. Always provide data_source_id.

Supported types: table, board, list, calendar, timeline, gallery, form, chart, map, and dashboard.

The optional configure field uses the view DSL for filters, sorts, grouping, and display. Read [REDACTED] through the MCP resource interface, or pass that URI to the Notion fetch tool. Do not guess the syntax.
tools.name: notion-create-view

tools.description:
Update a view's name, filters, sorts, or display configuration.

Use "fetch" to get view IDs from database responses. Only include fields
you want to change. The "configure" param uses the same DSL as create_view.
Use CLEAR to remove settings:
- CLEAR FILTER — remove all filters
- CLEAR QUICK FILTER — remove all quick filters, or name properties to remove only theirs (CLEAR QUICK FILTER "Status")
- CLEAR SORT — remove all sorts
- CLEAR GROUP BY — remove grouping. Boards reject it; use GROUP BY with another property instead (CLEAR SUB GROUP BY still works).
- CLEAR SUB GROUP BY — remove board sub-grouping
- CLEAR ICON — remove the view's tab icon
- CLEAR SUBSET FILTER — remove an XL view's subset filter


Set board or gallery card layout with CARD LAYOUT default or CARD LAYOUT compact. Set gallery card size without a cover property with CARD SIZE small, medium, or large. BY OPTION and BY GROUP apply only to status properties and rollups that return status values (Show original or Show unique). For select and multi_select properties, omit both modifiers, even if the property is named "Status" (for example, GROUP BY "Status").

See [REDACTED] resource for full syntax (readable via your MCP client's resource-reading interface, or by passing the URI to the Notion "fetch" tool).

<example description="Rename">{"view_id": "abc123", "name": "Sprint Board"}</example>
<example description="Update filter">{"view_id": "abc123", "configure": "FILTER "Status" = "Done""}</example>
<example description="Add quick filters without criteria">{"view_id": "abc123", "configure": "QUICK FILTER "Status", "Assignee""}</example>
<example description="Clear filter, add sort">{"view_id": "abc123", "configure": "CLEAR FILTER; SORT BY "Created" DESC"}</example>
<example description="Update grouping">{"view_id": "abc123", "configure": "GROUP BY "Status" BY GROUP SHOW EMPTY; SUB GROUP BY "Priority"; CARD LAYOUT compact"}</example>
tools.name: notion-update-view

tools.description: List what changed in a Notion page or database between two times, who changed it, and whether they used AI, an agent, or an MCP client. Each block, property, row, data source, or view that changed is listed once, with how it looked at the start and at the end of the time range. The range defaults to the last 24 hours. Filter by authors or sources to list only the records those people, agents, or kinds of edits touched; before and after still include everyone's edits, so use a shorter range to isolate one author. To read the whole page at a time, use view_version. Comments are not listed. Changes inside a page's inline databases are not listed either; pass an inline database's url to read them. Times are in UTC; convert them to the user's time zone before you show them. Requires edit access to the page.
tools.name: notion-get-version-changes

tools.description: Read a Notion page or database as it looked at a past time. The open page and other reads show only current content, so use this for any question about what a page said, contained, or looked like at an earlier date, even when the page is already open. A page returns its Markdown and properties; each inline database is a database tag, and you can pass that tag's url to this tool to read the database at the same time. A database returns its data sources, views, and rows. A linked database leaves out the data sources, views, and rows that belong to another database. Requires edit access to the page.
tools.name: notion-view-version

tools.description: Restore a whole Notion page or database to how it looked at a past time. This undoes every edit made after that time, including other people's, and removes comments added after it. To undo one change but keep later edits, edit the page instead. Before you call it, use get_version_changes from that time to now to see what will be undone, then list those changes for the user in your reply. The approval card does not list them. If the page has databases inside it and the user did not say whether to restore them, ask. If a restore is rejected or declined, do not make the same change another way, such as by editing the page. Tell the user what happened and ask what they want. Requires edit access. This tool only starts the restore, which then runs in the background, so the page can look unchanged for a short time. To undo a restore, restore the page to its started_at time.
tools.name: notion-restore-version

tools.description: List the pages that link to or mention a Notion page (backlinks), in the same workspace. Returns IDs, titles and URLs only; fetch a result to read it. Only pages you can open are listed. Follow next_cursor for more.
tools.name: notion-list-page-backlinks

tools.description: Get the current user's Notion sidebar tabs, in order, plus catalogs of the shortcuts and sections they can add. Shortcut groups are not returned or editable. Catalog examples are valid update_sidebar_tabs inputs, including configured New page shortcuts and database view sections. Each tab is independent: built-in items may appear in more than one tab. Call this before update_sidebar_tabs.
tools.name: notion-get-sidebar-tabs

tools.description: Replace the current user's complete, ordered Notion sidebar tab list. Use it to organize the sidebar around how the user works, for example a tab per workflow with its databases, teamspaces, and New page shortcuts. First call get_sidebar_tabs, then send back every tab, shortcut, and section to keep with its id. Omit an existing item to remove it, and omit id only for a new tab, configured shortcut, or database view section. Removing a tab also removes its shortcut groups. Rich objects describe their complete desired state, so omitting an optional field such as label, templateUrl, customName, openIn, or itemLimit clears it. Database view sections need a view:// URL or a Notion URL with a v= view id. Teamspace sections need a teamspace:// URL or a teamspace id from get_teams, for a teamspace the user has joined. Tab icons are Notion icon names such as home, checkmark-square, calendar, book, briefcase, people, inbox, folder, rocket, or chart-line. Check the returned config, and do not claim success unless the requested items are present.
tools.name: notion-update-sidebar-tabs

tools.description: Favorite or unfavorite 1 to 100 Notion pages or databases for the current user. Set favorited to true to add them or false to remove them. New favorites appear at the top in input order; existing favorites keep their position. To reorder, pass position (start, end, or after_page with another favorite's URL): the pages go there in input order, whether or not they were already favorites. Repeating the request is a no-op. All additions must be accessible in the current workspace; removals also work for inaccessible or deleted favorites. If additions are inaccessible, the error lists all failed URLs and nothing changes. Retry with the remaining URLs. This changes only the current user's Favorites, not page permissions.
tools.name: notion-update-page-favorites

tools.description: List calendars grouped by connected account. Use this to identify a target or conflict calendar before another Calendar operation.
tools.name: notion-calendar-list-calendars

tools.description: List the user's events across connected calendars within a time range. Use this to inspect the user's own schedule or identify events before changing them.
tools.name: notion-calendar-list-events

tools.description: List detailed events for coworkers in the same organization within a time range. Use this when event titles or context are needed, not only free/busy availability.
tools.name: notion-calendar-list-coworkers-events

tools.description: List rooms or other calendar resources available for specific times. Resource discovery is scoped to the connected account of the target calendar and only works with Google Workspace accounts that have admin permissions to view Calendar resources.
tools.name: notion-calendar-list-calendar-resources

tools.description: Find contacts by name or email across the user's connected Calendar accounts. Use this to resolve attendee identities before another Calendar operation.
tools.name: notion-calendar-list-contacts

tools.description: Create one or more events on writable calendars. Use this after the date, time, attendees, and target calendar are known. Creating events may notify attendees.
tools.name: notion-calendar-create-events

tools.description: Update one or more identified events, including timing, attendees, recurrence, resources, or RSVP status. Updates require permission and may notify attendees.
tools.name: notion-calendar-update-events

tools.description: Cancel one or more identified events the user can manage. Cancellation may notify attendees. For an event the user does not organize, use calendar_update_events with updateType: "RSVP" instead.
tools.name: notion-calendar-cancel-events

tools.description: Link an existing full-page meeting note to a calendar event. First find the event with the calendar tools. A meeting note embedded in a page appears as a <meeting-notes> tag: pass the URL from that tag, not the URL of the page around it. If the result lists otherMeetingNoteUrls, tell the user the event already has those meeting notes and link them. To create a new meeting note for an event, use create_meeting_note.
tools.name: notion-link-meeting-note-to-calendar-event

tools.description: Turn an existing regular database into a Meetings database, so its rows can be meeting notes. Existing rows are kept as they are. Only pass dateProperty or attendeesProperty when the user chose an existing property; otherwise a single matching property is reused and a missing one is created.
tools.name: notion-convert-to-meetings-database

tools.description: Create a Notion meeting note. Use this instead of create_pages whenever the user asks for a meeting note. content is written to the meeting note's Notes tab. Omit parent to file the note where the user's meeting notes go by default; pass parent only when the user names a destination. If parent is a regular database, not a Meetings database, first ask the user whether to convert it with convert_to_meetings_database. If the request refers to a scheduled meeting, first find it with the calendar tools and pass calendarEvent, without parent, title or content; if none matches, create the note without it. With calendarEvent, returns the event's meeting note (status "existing") or creates one filed and titled like the event's other notes; add content to it afterwards. Without calendarEvent, creates a new meeting note on every call.
tools.name: notion-create-meeting-note

tools.description: Returns Notion's setup guide for agents: how to set up Notion as the user's shared context and memory across agents. Call it when the user asks you to set up Notion or the Notion MCP, then follow the guide step by step with the user.
tools.name: notion-get-setup-guide
